definition: The ventral anterior cingulate cortex is a lower frontal part of the anterior cingulate cortex, near the subgenual region. In the supplied study, this area showed increased cerebral blood flow after short-term integrative body-mind training and was described as important for self-regulation.

reasons: The packet supports that short-term IBMT increased cerebral blood flow in the subgenual/adjacent ventral anterior cingulate cortex and that this region was described as critical for self-regulation, but it does not support the anatomical gloss that it is a "lower frontal part" of the anterior cingulate cortex.
The definition adds a location description near the subgenual region that is broader than the packet’s wording and is not independently supported by the supplied text.

The packet does not support the claim that the ventral anterior cingulate cortex is a “lower frontal part” of the anterior cingulate cortex; it only describes it as “subgenual/adjacent ventral anterior cingulate cortex.”
Because of the unsupported location phrasing, the definition contains at least one substantive claim not supported by the supplied packet.
